summary: No persistent Tasks/*.yaml graph exists yet. This snapshot proposes bootstrap seed records only; human approval and the deterministic Work Graph Seeder are required before any persistent task state is created.

proposed_seed_records.title: Mouse-Directed Player Movement, Shared Pointer Projection, and Movement Restriction

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Movement is mouse-directed: a click sets a destination the wizard walks toward, and holding continues steering toward the current cursor position, consumed through Unity Input System/Input Actions rather than direct hardware polling.

Exposes a shared world-space pointer target produced by projecting the cursor onto the gameplay plane, consumable by cursor-aimed spells and Door/Interaction without those systems independently projecting screen coordinates.

acceptance_criteria.reference: GDD §2 Player Movement ownership; §4 Development Agent Ownership Invariants
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled movement-restriction request/release interface that Charged Fireball can use to restrict movement while charging without Fireball mutating movement internals directly.

Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that restores player position/movement state to the floor's initial state, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator rather than having position mutated externally.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Victory/input-shutdown ownership bullet; Section 4 — Final escape/victory coordination invariant
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately stops or cancels any in-progress input-driven movement (including an active click-to-destination approach), rejects new movement commands while suspended, and is re-enabled only through an authorized reset/test flow; consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability rather than having movement internals mutated directly.

acceptance_criteria.reference: GDD §2 Victory/input-shutdown ownership; §4 Development Agent Ownership Invariants
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately stops already-active input-driven movement, rejects new movement commands while suspended, and can be re-enabled only through an authorized reset/test flow, consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability.

validation_requirements.requirement: Play Mode validation that clicking a location moves the wizard toward it and that holding steers continuously toward the live cursor position.
Validate that the exposed world-space pointer target is correctly consumable by a cursor-aimed spell or Door/Interaction integration once those systems exist.

Play Mode check: invoking the suspend interface while movement is active immediately halts the wizard's in-progress movement (including an active click-to-destination approach), and further movement input has no effect until an authorized re-enable/reset flow runs.

proposed_seed_records.title: Player Health Ownership, Restore, Death Transition, and Feedback

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled restore/heal entry point clamped to maximum health, to be requested by Door and Interaction's lock-and-heal behavior rather than Door writing health directly.
Exposes an observable zero-health/death transition (e.g. an event) that the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator can consume without polling health each frame or mutating Player Health internals.
Provides a continuous player-facing health indicator reflecting current/maximum health at all times.
Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point restoring current health to its floor-initial value, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

Health does not passively regenerate during or between rooms; it changes only through the owner-controlled damage interface, the owner-controlled restore interface (door-lock recovery), or the orchestrator-invoked floor reset.

validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that failure is readable through health/damage feedback (contributing cause alongside positioning, mana, and timing failures).
Failure caused by poor positioning is readable to the player through health/damage feedback, as part of the required 'failure is readable' success criterion.

proposed_seed_records.title: Player Mana Ownership, Restart Reset, and Denied-Cast Feedback

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that restores current mana to full and clears post-cast regeneration-delay timer state for floor restart.

acceptance_criteria.reference: GDD §3 Player Experience Success Criteria — Failure is readable
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes a signal (e.g. an event) when a cast attempt is denied due to insufficient mana, distinct from a successful spend, so a consuming spell/UI can present readable low-mana feedback; exact presentation is an implementation choice.
Continues to own only current mana and post-cast regeneration-delay state; does not absorb Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave spell-local cooldown, charge, cast, placement, or active-field state.

validation_requirements.requirement: Existing Play Mode coverage of Spend/regen/post-cast-delay behavior (PlayerManaPlayModeTests.cs) continues to pass and is extended to cover the new reset entry point and denied-cast signal.
Validate that failure is readable through low-mana feedback as one of the stated readable failure causes.
Failure caused by low mana is readable to the player through the mana indicator, as part of the required 'failure is readable' success criterion.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Player Actions and Systems, Fireball row
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Tap-cast produces a quick, mobile, cursor-aimed shot suited to a single or separated enemy; hold-to-charge costs more mana, restricts movement further, and deals area damage effective against clustered enemies.

While charging, Fireball requests the charging movement restriction through an owner-controlled Player Movement interface and releases it when charging ends/cancels/fires; Fireball never mutates Player Movement internals directly.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Resources, Feedback, and Failure / Development Agent Ownership Invariants
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Fireball spends mana for both tap and charge casts through Player Mana's existing owner-controlled Spend interface, with charge costing more than tap.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership bullet
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Fireball damages enemies only by requesting damage through the Enemy Health/Defeat owner-controlled damage interface; it does not write enemy health directly.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Player Movement ownership / Runtime Implementation
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Fireball consumes the shared world-space pointer target exposed by Player Movement for cursor aiming rather than independently projecting screen coordinates.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 5 — Runtime Implementation / Section 2 Player Movement ownership bullet
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Fireball's casting input (tap/charge/release) is routed through the project's Unity Input System/Input Actions layer rather than independent direct hardware polling.

Fireball owns its tap/charge/cast state and exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point for that state, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator, so no residual charge/cast state survives a floor restart.

Fireball exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately stops active charging/casting, rejects new cast input while suspended, and can be re-enabled by an authorized reset/test flow, consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions table / Section 3 Ruined Entry tactical purpose
validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that a full charge produces meaningful area damage against multiple naturally-clustering pursuing Melee Enemies, not just a single target, and that charging is interruptible/unsafe once enemies close distance.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions, Charged Fireball vs Ranged row
validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that a tap shot remains usable against a Ranged Enemy's telegraphed attack pattern where a full charge is impractical.
Validate that triggering a floor restart while Fireball is mid-charge/mid-cast clears that state through Fireball's own reset entry point rather than leaving residual charge/cooldown state.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Player Actions and Systems / Frost Field targeting and feedback bullet
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Frost Field places its temporary slow area at the current shared world-space pointer target exposed by Player Movement, without independently projecting screen-to-world coordinates.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Frost Field targeting and feedback bullet
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Frost Field provides player-facing feedback that makes the cast and the active field readable during placement and while active; the exact visual/audio treatment is an implementation choice.

Frost Field triggers the enemy slowdown effect through the Enemy Pursuit/status-effect owner-controlled interface; it does not itself implement enemy slowdown application, restoration, Ranged Enemy targeting, or Ranged Enemy attacks.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Resources, Feedback, and Failure / Development Agent Ownership Invariants
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Frost Field spends mana through Player Mana's existing owner-controlled Spend interface when cast.
Frost Field's casting input is routed through the project's Unity Input System/Input Actions layer rather than independent direct hardware polling.
Frost Field owns its Wizard-Combat-side cast/placement/active-field state and exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point for that state, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

Frost Field exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately stops active casting/placement, rejects new cast input while suspended, and can be re-enabled by an authorized reset/test flow, consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions, Frost Field row
validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that casting Frost Field creates a readable opening against a melee group (stretches pursuit) without itself guaranteeing a fully safe Fireball charge in every position, matching the resource-tradeoff description.
Validate that triggering a floor restart while a Frost Field cast/placement is active clears Frost Field's own casting-side state through its reset entry point.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Player Actions and Systems, Force Wave row
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Force Wave is a player-centered short-range radial knockback that does not use cursor direction or target selection, with a long cooldown limiting reuse.

Each cast spends 25 mana (initial tuning value) through Player Mana's existing owner-controlled Spend interface and starts Force Wave's own visible long cooldown; the cast is refused if the spend fails.

Force Wave determines which enemies within its radius are affected and requests the radial knockback displacement through the Enemy Pursuit/status-effect-displacement owner-controlled interface; Force Wave does not directly move enemies or manipulate their navigation/pursuit state.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 5 — Runtime Implementation / Section 2 Player Movement ownership bullet
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Force Wave's cast input is routed through the project's Unity Input System/Input Actions layer rather than independent direct hardware polling.
Force Wave owns its cooldown state and exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point for that state, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

Force Wave exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately stops any current cast activity, rejects new cast input while suspended, and can be re-enabled by an authorized reset/test flow, consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions, Force Wave row
validation_requirements.requirement: Validate Force Wave functions as an effective emergency response against a surrounding melee cluster or a group blocking a door, and confirm its short range makes it ineffective against distant Ranged Enemy pressure.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 2 — Design Pillars / narrative resource-tension text
validation_requirements.requirement: Validate the cooldown is long enough that an encounter space typically allows only about one meaningful Force Wave use, matching the intended resource-decision tension (spend mid-room vs. save for the door).
Validate that triggering a floor restart while Force Wave's cooldown is active clears the cooldown through Force Wave's own reset entry point.
Failure caused by using Force Wave without an immediate threat and then lacking it during a later critical moment, due to its long cooldown, is readable to the player.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Registry exposes the current active enemy count and remaining capacity under the hard cap of fifteen active enemies.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Enemy activation registers an enemy; only a defeat-driven unregister call (consumed by Enemy Health/Defeat) removes an enemy from the active count.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Target loss, entering search state, crossing between rooms, and waiting behind a locked door do not remove a surviving persistent enemy from the registry.

Registry exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that returns bookkeeping to the floor's initial state; the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator invokes this rather than mutating registry internals directly.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Win and Loss Conditions (Loss); Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
acceptance_criteria.requirement: After a floor restart, the registry's reported active count and remaining capacity agree with the set of live persistent enemies restored by the enemy-owned resets: an enemy restored to an active state is represented through the normal activation-registration path rather than being independently counted or omitted by restart-side adjustment, so admission gating resumes from accurate bookkeeping.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
validation_requirements.requirement: Verify the registry's reported active count and remaining capacity stay accurate as enemies are registered and unregistered, including at the fifteen-enemy hard cap boundary.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
validation_requirements.requirement: Verify target loss, search-state transition, room crossing, and waiting behind a locked door do not remove a surviving enemy from the registry's active count.

Verify floor restart returns registry bookkeeping to the floor's initial state through its owner-controlled reset entry point, and that the post-restart active count matches the live set of persistent enemies restored to their initial AI state rather than assuming an empty registry.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled damage-intake interface that any canon-required damage source (e.g. Fireball) calls rather than writing enemy health directly.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Reaching zero health triggers a defeat transition exactly once for that persistent enemy object.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Defeat reports removal through the Active Enemy Registry's owner-controlled unregister interface rather than the Enemy Health/Defeat component independently decrementing a separate count.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that restores health and clears the defeat transition for floor restart, invoked by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator rather than by direct internal mutation.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 1 — Executive Summary; Section 3 — Active Enemy Registry and Encounter Admission
acceptance_criteria.requirement: The defeat transition ends the enemy's participation as an active threat: its pursuit/attack behavior stops and it leaves play, while it remains the same persistent object restorable through the owner-controlled reset entry point.

A persistent enemy's health and defeat state changes only through the owner-controlled damage interface and the floor-restart reset entry point; it is never reinitialized or otherwise mutated by room transition, target loss, search, or doorway crossing.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
validation_requirements.requirement: Verify a damage source can only reduce a persistent enemy's health through the owner-controlled damage interface and that zero health triggers the defeat transition exactly once.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 3 — Enemy health and defeat ownership
validation_requirements.requirement: Verify defeat reports removal through the Active Enemy Registry's unregister interface without the registry double-counting or the two systems maintaining duplicate bookkeeping.
Verify floor restart returns a previously-damaged/defeated enemy's health and defeat state to its initial value through the owner-controlled reset entry point.
Verify a defeated enemy's pursuit/attack behavior stops and it leaves play immediately following the defeat transition, while remaining restorable via the floor-restart reset entry point.

Verify a persistent enemy's health/defeat state remains unchanged across room transitions, target loss, search, and doorway crossings, changing only through the damage interface or the reset entry point.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions (Frost Field row)
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Frost Field slowdown modifies an affected enemy's locomotion/repositioning speed only; it must never suppress, pause, or slow a Ranged Enemy's attack execution/timing.
Frost slowdown is restored (movement speed returns to normal) when the effect ends, with no permanent slowdown remaining.
Applies forced displacement requested by an ability (e.g. Force Wave's radial knockback selection) to the affected enemy while preserving valid movement/navigation state.

After displacement or Frost slowdown ends, returns the affected enemy to the appropriate pursuit/search movement state per the pursuit/search state contract, rather than defining a second enemy-state machine.
Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that clears any active Frost slowdown or displacement state for floor restart, invoked by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

validation_requirements.requirement: Verify Frost Field slowdown applies to a pursuing enemy's movement speed and is fully restored when the effect ends, with no permanent slowdown remaining (Unity Validation Agent concern in Section 4).

Verify forced displacement (e.g. Force Wave knockback) moves an affected enemy while preserving valid navigation/movement state and that the enemy resumes appropriate pursuit/search behavior afterward rather than becoming stuck.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 2 — Spell and Enemy Interactions (Frost Field row)
validation_requirements.requirement: Verify a Ranged Enemy under active Frost slowdown continues executing its telegraphed attack on schedule while only its repositioning speed is reduced.
Verify floor restart clears any active Frost slowdown or displacement state on all enemies through the owner-controlled reset entry point.

proposed_seed_records.title: Enemy Detection, Pursuit, and Search/Reacquisition Foundation

acceptance_criteria.reference: Enemy Detection, Pursuit, and Target Loss
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Detection Distance is strictly smaller than Lose Target Distance so acquisition/loss does not oscillate at one boundary.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Enemy Detection, Pursuit, and Target Loss
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Entering Detection Distance acquires the wizard and begins pursuit; crossing an open doorway does not by itself clear an acquired target.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Enemy Detection, Pursuit, and Target Loss
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exceeding Lose Target Distance transitions to a search state directed at the player's last known position using the distance threshold, not randomness, to decide the transition.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Enemy Detection, Pursuit, and Target Loss
acceptance_criteria.requirement: On reaching the last-known position without reacquisition, perform a short, bounded search/wander using controlled randomness over navigable points, periodically re-checking for the player; re-entering Detection Distance during this state reacquires the player.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Enemy Detection, Pursuit, and Target Loss
acceptance_criteria.requirement: If bounded search completes without reacquisition, clear the target and return to local idle/wander; the enemy remains the same persistent object and is not despawned, replaced, or reset.

A pursuing/searching enemy can continue forward traversal through an open or broken doorway when the shared navigation/locomotion passability result permits it, without losing its target solely because of the crossing.
Enemy locomotion consumes the shared gameplay navigation/locomotion layer's walkable movement representation rather than selecting or configuring navigation technology independently.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Floor-run restart ownership (Win and Loss Conditions)
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled restart/reset entry point that returns the enemy to its authored encounter/spawn region and clears all target/last-known-position/search state, for consumption by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator (owned by a different domain).

validation_requirements.requirement: Target-loss hysteresis/search and reacquisition Play Mode validation.
Bone Archive lane-pathing validation confirming enemy movement/navigation fits the room's described narrow-lane geometry.
Verify a tracking/pursuing or searching enemy follows the player or last-known position through an open/broken doorway without spuriously clearing its target solely due to the crossing.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Runs at the wizard and attacks at close range once the shared pursuit foundation acquires the player as target.
Deals damage to the player exclusively through the shared Player Health damage interface (existing PlayerHealth.TakeDamage), never writing separate player-health state.
A retreating player cannot maintain indefinite safety through ordinary movement alone; Melee Enemy pursuit gradually closes distance over time, with exact speed/tuning left to playtesting.

Multiple simultaneously pursuing Melee Enemies exhibit natural clustering while chasing (not rigid uniform spacing), preserving the relevance of Charged Fireball area damage and Frost Field formation-stretching.

Delivers a usable assembled world-space SpriteRenderer archetype prefab integrating the shared pursuit/locomotion foundation, Enemy Health/Defeat participation, Active Enemy Registry participation, and Melee attack behavior.

Exposes an owner-controlled attack-state reset entry point that clears any in-progress attack cooldown/windup and cancels an in-flight melee attack when the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator invokes floor restart, so no mid-execution attack state carries over from a failed run.
Exposes an owner-controlled restart/reset entry point that clears melee attack execution/wind-up state for floor restart, invoked by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator rather than mutated directly.

validation_requirements.requirement: Exercise multiple simultaneously pursuing Melee Enemies (not only one) to validate that clustering behavior remains meaningful for area-damage/formation-stretch interactions.
Verify melee damage is applied only through PlayerHealth.TakeDamage and not through any duplicated health-writing path.
Verify a mid-windup/mid-swing Melee Enemy attack is cancelled and cooldown/windup state is cleared by floor restart, with no attack state surviving into the next run.
Verify floor restart clears melee attack execution/wind-up state through the owner-controlled reset entry point.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Keeps moderate distance from the player and fires a slow, telegraphed ranged shot rather than an instantaneous attack.
Attack includes a line-of-sight/projectile-occlusion check so cover (e.g., Chapel of Ash pews/columns) actually blocks shots.
Deals damage to the player exclusively through the shared Player Health damage interface (existing PlayerHealth.TakeDamage).
Functions correctly as a standalone pursuer if it ends up fighting without Melee support, without requiring melee presence to operate.
Frost Field slowdown affects only the Ranged Enemy's repositioning/locomotion speed and does not suppress, pause, or otherwise slow its telegraphed attack execution.

Delivers a usable assembled world-space SpriteRenderer archetype prefab integrating the shared pursuit/locomotion foundation (moderate-distance keep-away behavior), Enemy Health/Defeat participation, Active Enemy Registry participation, and Ranged attack/occlusion behavior.

Exposes an owner-controlled attack-state reset entry point that clears any in-progress telegraphed-shot windup and cancels/despawns any in-flight projectile when the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator invokes floor restart, so no mid-execution attack state carries over from a failed run.

Exposes an owner-controlled restart/reset entry point that clears ranged attack/telegraph timing and any in-flight projectile state for floor restart, invoked by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator rather than mutated directly.

validation_requirements.reference: Dungeon Floor Structure (Chapel of Ash) / Development Agent Roles (Unity Validation Agent)
validation_requirements.requirement: Chapel of Ash line-of-sight/projectile-occlusion Play Mode validation confirming cover blocks shots.
Verify a slowed (Frost Field) Ranged Enemy continues its normal telegraphed attack behavior while its repositioning speed is reduced.
Verify an in-progress telegraphed shot or in-flight projectile is cancelled/cleared by floor restart, with no attack state surviving into the next run.
Verify floor restart clears ranged attack/telegraph timing and any in-flight projectile state through the owner-controlled reset entry point.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: A surviving enemy still actively tracking/pursuing the player and whose route is blocked by a newly locked door begins attacking that door; no separate 'witnessed escape' or line-of-sight-to-crossing flag is tracked.
An enemy that has already lost the player (cleared target) does not attack a locked door merely because it is nearby.
The attack requests door damage exclusively through the Door-owned damage-receive interface and never writes door durability or semantic door state directly.

When the door breaks (transitions to broken), the still-tracking/pursuing enemy continues pursuit forward through the now-passable doorway using the shared navigation/locomotion passability result, without independently manipulating door or navigation state.

Exposes an owner-controlled attack-state reset entry point that cancels any in-progress locked-door attack attempt when the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator invokes floor restart, so no partially-executed door-attack state carries over from the failed run.

Exposes an owner-controlled restart/reset entry point that clears locked-door attack initiation/in-progress state for floor restart, invoked by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator rather than mutated directly.

validation_requirements.reference: Dungeon Floor Structure (Lower Vault) / Door and Pursuit Rules
validation_requirements.requirement: Verify that after a rear breach, locked-door-attacking pursuers correctly resume forward pursuit through the broken doorway rather than stalling.
Verify an enemy that has already lost the player (post bounded-search target clear) does not initiate a locked-door attack solely from proximity.
The player understands that enemies left alive remain a threat: leaving them alive means locking a door while they attack it, and later encountering them if that door breaks through.
Verify an in-progress locked-door attack attempt is cancelled and cleared by floor restart, with no door-attack state surviving into the next run.
Verify floor restart clears locked-door attack initiation/in-progress state through the owner-controlled reset entry point.

proposed_seed_records.title: Cursor-Targeted Door Opening (Click-to-Approach, Arm's-Reach Auto-Timer, Interruption)

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Clicking a sealed door issues a combined approach-and-interact request using the shared world-space pointer target exposed by Player Movement; Door and Interaction does not independently project screen-to-world coordinates.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Open Sealed Door; Section 3 — Door and Pursuit Rules
acceptance_criteria.requirement: The wizard automatically moves to the door's interaction position; when arm's-reach range is reached, the five-second opening timer starts automatically with no sustained button hold required.
After the door is selected, cursor movement/drift away from the door does not cancel the approach request or the running timer.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Setbacks; Section 3 — Door and Pursuit Rules
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Taking damage, moving away once timing has begun, or issuing another command that cancels/replaces the door interaction resets progress to zero.
Door selection/approach input is consumed through the project's Unity Input System/Input Actions layer rather than independent direct hardware polling.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Victory/input-shutdown ownership; Section 4 — Final escape/victory coordination; Section 5 — Runtime Implementation (Game Flow/Victory capability)
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately cancels an in-progress door approach/opening timer, rejects new door-selection commands while suspended, and can be re-enabled only through an authorized reset/test flow.

Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that returns its owned interaction/opening state (opening progress, interacting flag, open flag, and doorway-blocker state) to floor-initial values, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 2 — Open Sealed Door; Section 3 — Door Passability Contract
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Completing five uninterrupted seconds transitions the door's semantic state from sealed to open (player-traversable); door-close-lock-break-lifecycle owns publishing this resulting open state through the shared navigation-owned passability interface.

Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point that returns owned opening state (interaction progress, open flag, doorway-blocker enablement) to floor-initial values, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator rather than having internals mutated externally.

acceptance_criteria.reference: GDD §2 Victory/input-shutdown ownership; §4 Development Agent Ownership Invariants
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes an owner-controlled gameplay-enable/suspend interface that immediately stops an in-progress door approach/opening timer, rejects new door-interaction commands while suspended, and can be re-enabled only through an authorized reset/test flow, consumed by the Game Flow/Victory capability.

validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that a first-time player understands reaching the door alone is insufficient and that the automatic five-second timer must complete uninterrupted.

validation_requirements.reference: Section 4 — Unity Validation Agent row; Example Game-Specific Agent Task
validation_requirements.requirement: Validate cursor-targeted door range and cursor-drift behavior: drift after selection does not cancel, while damage/moving away during timing does.
A first-time player understands that clicking a door sends the wizard to it, and that reaching the door is not enough — the automatic opening timer still requires five safe, uninterrupted seconds.

Door interaction requires accurate cursor target selection only on the initial click; the wizard's automatic approach, the timer's automatic start on arrival, and tolerance of normal cursor drift after selection are all readable to a first-time player.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Detects, for an open door, when the wizard has actually crossed to that door's forward side; opening the door alone does not set crossing state.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 4 — Door and Interaction Agent row
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes the crossing state/event through a stable owner-side interface consumed by door close/lock and final-escape victory, so those consumers do not implement their own crossing detector.
Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point for its crossing state, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that crossing is detected only after the door is open and the wizard has reached the forward side, not merely on interaction completion.

proposed_seed_records.title: Door Close/Lock, Health Restore Request, Durability, and Locked-to-Broken Lifecycle

acceptance_criteria.requirement: After doorway-crossing-state confirms forward-side crossing, the door automatically closes and locks with no additional player input.

Completing the automatic close/lock requests the small fixed health restoration through the Player Health owner-controlled restore interface (clamped to max health); this component never writes Player Health state directly.
Once locked, the door cannot be reopened, unlocked, or crossed again by the player; the floor is a forward-only escape sequence, including after any door has broken.

acceptance_criteria.reference: Section 3 — Locked-door attack and durability ownership
acceptance_criteria.requirement: Exposes runtime durability and an owner-controlled damage-receive interface that other systems (e.g., enemy locked-door attacks) call to reduce durability; owns the locked-to-broken state transition; requesting systems never write durability or semantic door state directly.

When durability reaches zero the door breaks; a broken door remains open and cannot be closed or relocked for the remainder of the run, permits forward enemy traversal, and is not a return path for the player.

Publishes semantic door state (sealed/open/locked/broken) through the shared navigation-owned passability interface so sealed/locked blocks enemy traversal and open/broken permits it; this component does not directly manipulate NavMesh or doorway passability itself.
Provides required player-facing breach feedback — banging, shaking, cracks, and a durability indicator — as the door nears breaking; this is implementation behavior, not validation-only prose.
Exposes an owner-controlled reset entry point for door lifecycle/crossing/durability state, consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

Exposes a per-door authorable/serialized durability value so Dungeon Encounter can configure it per door, without Dungeon Encounter owning runtime durability state, damage intake, or the locked-to-broken transition.

validation_requirements.requirement: Validate that a surviving enemy still actively tracking/pursuing the player and blocked by the locked door continues attacking it until it breaks, and that pursuit resumes through the doorway once broken (exercised jointly with the enemy_behavior domain's locked-door attack owner).
Validate that a broken or locked door is never a return path for the player, including after breaking.
Validate that breach feedback (banging/shaking/crack/durability indicator) is player-perceivable before the door actually breaks.
Crossing an opened doorway causes automatic close-and-lock with no second player input required, and this behavior is readable/expected by a first-time player.
Failure caused by waiting too long — allowing a locked door to break under sustained pursuer pressure — is readable to the player through durability/breach feedback.
